me.json.description: Finding your own name, what is in your stack, and what you are allowed to change.

me.description: Long sections of aos/me.json kept as their own files (self_tools, self_llm, self_system, self_history, do_task, self_hook); aos/me.json points to each with $ref.

errors.json.description: How to read a failed call: the `error:` line, `warning:` lines, and exit codes.

errors.description: Long sections of aos/errors.json kept as their own files (common); aos/errors.json points to it with $ref.

world.json.description: The mental model: daemon = hardware, stack = memory, workspace = external memory, definition = source code, kernel = where you send requests.

definition.json.description: What each file in a definition folder does (interfaces.json, loop.json, tools.json, hooks.json, cli.json ...), and which ones you have your own copy of.

body.json.description: Two kinds of body, agent-fsm and eca (claude, codex): brain, tools, hooks, system text, history; how to tell which you are.

status.json.description: The daemon table, the phases an agent can be in, and what each phase means for you.

brain.json.description: How a brain request travels, what an endpoint pack is, and how priority works.

agents.json.description: Tools subagent, agents_ctl, agent_def and fork: your own subagents, any agent on the daemon table, new definitions, and a copy of yourself for one goal.

agents.description: Long sections of aos/agents.json kept as their own files (subagent, fork); aos/agents.json points to each with $ref.

rules.json.description: What you must not do, and why. Read this before doing anything that changes the system.

knowledge.json.description: Describes the former knowledge_read / knowledge_write tools (removed 11-12); kept as is.

cli.description: Use these shell commands to manage agents, tools and daemon procs.

mailbox.json.description: Letters between agents: tools mailbox_peek, mailbox_read, mailbox_send; when you must answer; checking regularly without filling your history.

clock.json.description: Timers: clock letters to your queue (clock_register), or an on_clock hook that adds nothing to your history; which one to choose.

tools_def.json.description: Making your own tools: tool tools_def (new from the Python skeleton, check) and the Python helper tool_spec.

tools.description: One node per stock tool (read, ls, write, edit, trash, shell ...): when to use it and which tool instead, examples with real output, errors.

packs.json.description: Your tools come in packs (look, change, delete, shell, gadgets, events, todo, self, subagent, def, mailbox, knowledge, goal): one sentence per tool, and how a pack is turned off.

_description.json.description: aos in one page: what aos is, the eight words, five rules, and how to look up more (that last part still names knowledge_read / knowledge_write).

kernel.json.description: What a kernel is (resource management and scheduling, seen from the sender), where to send requests, the example kernels, and how to write your own.
